summary.name: aria2
summary.one_liner: aria2 is a lightweight, multi-protocol, multi-source command-line download utility that also includes a BitTorrent client and JSON-RPC/XML-RPC control interfaces.
use_cases: Speed up a large file download by using multiple connections
Download files over HTTP, FTP or SFTP from the terminal
Download BitTorrent torrents or magnet links from the command line
Batch download URIs listed in a text file
Control a running download process remotely via RPC
Scripted downloads with low memory and CPU use
summary.what_it_does: aria2 downloads files from HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SFTP, BitTorrent and Metalink sources, and can combine multiple sources or connections to use maximum available bandwidth. It works as a full BitTorrent client with DHT, PEX, encryption, magnet URIs, web-seeding, selective downloads, local peer discovery and UDP trackers. It supports Metalink v4, Metalink v3 and Metalink/HTTP, including file verification. The process can be controlled through built-in JSON-RPC (over HTTP and WebSocket) and XML-RPC interfaces. The page says it uses about 4 MiB of memory for normal HTTP/FTP downloads and up to 9 MiB for BitTorrent.
notable: Multi-connection downloads that combine multiple sources or protocols
Full BitTorrent client with DHT, PEX, encryption and magnet URI support
Metalink v4, v3 and Metalink/HTTP support with file verification
Remote control via JSON-RPC (HTTP and WebSocket) and XML-RPC
caveats: Command-line only; graphical interfaces are separate third-party frontends such as webui-aria2 and uGet
Released under GPL v2 or later, per the license section
